justification: Mechanical gate is clean: Lighthouse 100/100/100/100, 0 console errors, 0 broken internal links, 0px mobile overflow (gate.json, checked 2026-09-24T20:44:24Z, run fresh this round). I opened every desktop-light and mobile-dark screenshot (fold + all 11 / all 16 parts respectively) plus the fold and two body parts each of desktop-dark (part04, part08) and mobile-light (part06, part12). Heading hierarchy (6 h2s, no h3s, matching the 6 sections) is clean and consistent with sibling database articles. Code blocks render correctly in both themes with working copy buttons and distinct dark output panels; the collapsed <details> 'Show solution' pattern is used for all three exercises in both themes, styled as a green-accented callout, and never spoils an answer above the fold. Figure 1 (concatenation vs. bound parameter) is the one diagram the CONTENT_PLAN row calls for; it has a real title/desc, red/bad vs green/good boxes that stay correctly colored and legible at 390px in mobile-dark-part07 and mobile-light-part12, and a caption that states what to notice. I re-fetched two of the pages that currently rank for the target query as fresh comparisons this round: Microsoft's own SQL Server injection guide (a dense text-and-table wall, static non-runnable C#/SQL snippets, no dark mode, no diagrams beyond two small reference tables) and StackHawk's .NET SQL injection guide (a light-only marketing page with static, non-executable snippets and no interactive elements at all). Neither comes close to this article's runnable code + verified output panels + working dark theme + collapsible exercises + custom diagram, which is what a 9+ requires rather than an assumed pass. I then opened all three round-1 reviews. The two round-1 design issues (mobile code-block horizontal scroll on long ADO.NET lines; byline rendering as the site name rather than a person) are both explicitly scoped to the integrator/owner, not the writer, and both are unchanged and still visible this round (confirmed directly in the mobile-dark and mobile-light screenshots opened above) -- carried forward rather than double-counted as new findings. The round-1 technical and adsense fixes (CWE-89 ordering claim, missing batching citation, the trimmed Microsoft SQL Server quote) were all textual/citation changes with no visual side effects, and none introduced a new design regression: word count, section count, and screenshot part counts are essentially unchanged from round 1.

issues.location: Every C# code block, mobile viewport (e.g. mobile-dark-part02, mobile-light-part06)
issues.problem: Almost every run block still has lines well past the ~40-character width visible at 390px before horizontal scrolling kicks in (e.g. the CREATE TABLE / INSERT concatenation lines), so a mobile reader scrolls sideways inside nearly every snippet on the page. Unchanged from round 1.
issues.fixLooksLike: Not a per-article fix: this is the shell's code-block behavior applied to genuinely long ADO.NET call chains. If it recurs across the pillar's SQL/ADO.NET articles, the integrator could consider a slightly smaller mobile code font-size step, or the writer could break a few of the longest concatenation lines (e.g. the CREATE TABLE strings) earlier so the operative keyword is visible without scrolling.

issues.location: Front matter byline, rendered in the page header ('By Computer Science Guide') on every screenshot
issues.problem: The byline still renders as the site name rather than a person, on every article checked so far in this pillar; on this specific security-focused article a named, credentialed byline would read as slightly more trustworthy to a reader evaluating whether to trust the exploit code. Unchanged from round 1.
issues.fixLooksLike: No change needed for this article alone (this is the site-wide author-display pattern, and a real byline is an owner-level NEEDS_MARKUS decision, not something this article should invent). Flagging only in case the owner wants a consistent policy across the security-adjacent articles.
